questions.stem: What would the government do with regard to artificial grass?

options.A: Urge legislation to restrict its use.
options.B: Take measures to guarantee its quality.
options.C: Remind its users to obey existing rules.

questions.answerZh: 提醒使用者遵守现有规定
basis: 第五段政府明确表态不打算禁用假草；第六段说更愿意帮人们做出正确选择，而不是立法；接着 However 一转：使用人造草必须遵守现行的（in place）法律和政策保障。这就是提醒使用者遵守已有规定。
map: must comply with
obey
the legal and policy safeguards in place
existing rules

wrong.text: 政府说的是 rather than legislating，不打算立法限制。
没提保证假草质量。
原文是鼓励公共机构“考虑”可持续替代方案（consider sustainable alternatives），不是政府要用替代品取代假草。

context.text: … About eight million square metres of plastic grass is sold each year but ==**opposition** has now spread to the highest gardening circles==. The Chelsea Flower Show has banned fake grass from this year’s event, declaring it to be not part of its ethos. The Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), which runs the annual show in west London, says it has introduced the ban because of the damage plastic grass does to the environment and biodiversity.
==However, **supporters of fake grass** point out== that there is also an environmental impact with natural lawns, which need mowing and therefore usually consume electricity or petrol. …

questions.stem: It can be learned from the text that fake grass ______.

options.B: has seen a market share decline

basis: 全文主旨题。一方是反对者：RHS 禁止参展、活动人士发起请愿、要求禁售和征税；另一方是支持者：行业指出真草也有环境代价；政府则不禁止、只要求守规。有人反对、有人支持，假草就是一个有争议的产品。
map: opposition … / supporters of fake grass …
controversial

wrong.text: 全文没有讲假草在技术上不断改进。
只说每年卖出约八百万平方米，没有市场份额下降的数据。
没有讲价格；£500 是铺假草的人买树木灌木的花费，与假草价格无关。

context.text: But the government is right about one thing: U.S. national parks are in crisis. ==Collectively, they have a **maintenance backlog** of more than $12 billion.== ==Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other **infrastructure are crumbling**.==

questions.stem: What problem are U.S. national parks faced with?
basis: 第二段直接说国家公园处于危机中：维护工作积压的资金缺口超过 120 亿美元，道路、步道、卫生间、游客中心等基础设施正在破败。维护积压、设施破败，就是基础设施维护不善。
map: maintenance backlog / infrastructure are crumbling
poorly maintained infrastructure

wrong.text: 第三段说公园里的企业只把约 5% 的收入交给管理局，讲的是上交比例低，不是企业利润下降。
作者恰恰反对靠商业化解决问题，认为它不是万能药，还会破坏游客体验。
亚马逊送快递到帐篷是政府被嘲讽的点子，不是说公园缺交通服务。

context.text: … ==increased privatization would certainly **undercut** one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: **to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat** that overwhelms daily life.==

questions.stem: Increased privatization of the campgrounds may ______.
basis: 第四段：加大私有化必然会削弱（undercut）游客来公园的主要原因之一，即享受自然、暂时摆脱日常生活里铺天盖地的商业气息。来公园的目的被破坏，就是游客体验被破坏。
map: undercut
spoil
to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat
visitor experience

wrong.text: 私有化会让人难以享受自然，不是有助于保护自然。
没有提运营压力。
削弱了游客来访的理由，不会促进访问量。

context.text: … An economic survey of 700 U.S. taxpayers found that people would be willing to pay a significant amount of money to make sure the parks and their programs are kept intact. ==**Some 81% of respondents** said they would be **willing to pay additional taxes** for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts to the national parks.==

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 5, most respondents in the survey would ______.

options.A: go to the national parks on a regular basis
options.B: advocate a bigger budget for the national parks
options.C: agree to pay extra for the national parks
options.D: support the national parks’ recent reforms

questions.answerZh: 同意为国家公园额外付费
basis: 第五段调查：约 81% 的受访者（most respondents）表示愿意在今后 10 年多缴税，以免国家公园经费被削减。愿意多缴税就是同意为国家公园额外付费。
map: Some 81% of respondents
most respondents
willing to pay additional taxes
agree to pay extra

wrong.text: 调查问的是愿不愿意出钱，不是会不会经常去。
受访者说的是自己愿意多付钱，不是倡导国会扩大预算。增加预算是作者在最后一段暗示的结论，不是受访者的表态。
文中没提公园最近有什么改革。

context.text: … ==The parks also help **keep America’s past alive**, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to **protect historical sites**== and to bring the stories of these places to life.

questions.stem: The national parks are valuable in that they ______.

options.D: provide an income for the locals

basis: 第六段逐项列公园的价值，最后一句：公园还帮助让美国的过去“活着”，与各地合作保护历史遗迹、讲述这些地方的故事。这就是具有历史意义。
map: keep America’s past alive / protect historical sites
have historical significance

wrong.text: 旅游只是公园产生价值的途径之一（of course through tourism），没说公园在旅游业中领先。
原文是公园通过固碳对气候有积极影响，不是资助气候研究。
与地方管辖机构合作是为了保护历史遗迹，没说给当地人提供收入。

context.text: ==The real problem is that the parks have been **chronically starved of funding**.== …

==The parks do all this **on a shoestring**.== Congress allocates only $3 billion a year to the national park system—==an amount that has been **flat** since 2001== (in inflation-adjusted dollars) with the exception of a onetime boost in 2009. Meanwhile, ==the number of annual visitors has **increased by more than 50%** since 1980==, and now stands at 330 million visitors per year.

questions.stem: It can be concluded from the text that the national park system ______.

options.A: is able to cope with staff shortages
options.B: is able to meet visitors’ demands
options.C: is in need of a new pricing policy
options.D: is in need of a funding increase

basis: 第五段点明真正的问题是公园长期缺钱（chronically starved of funding）。最后一段又说公园靠极少的钱（on a shoestring）做这么多事：国会拨款自 2001 年起基本没涨，游客却比 1980 年多了 50% 以上。钱不涨、人在涨，结论就是需要增加资金。
map: chronically starved of funding / on a shoestring
in need of a funding increase

wrong.text: 全文没有提员工短缺。
基础设施在破败、游客在增加、经费却不涨，说明难以满足游客需求。
没有讨论门票或定价；调查讲的是多缴税。

context.text: ==The Internet may be **changing merely what we remember**, **not our capacity** to do so==, suggests Columbia University psychology professor Betsy Sparrow. In 2011, Sparrow led a study in which participants were asked to record 40 factoids in a computer (“an ostrich’s eye is bigger than its brain,” for example). Half of the participants were told the information would be erased, while the other half were told it would be saved. Guess what? The latter group made no effort to recall the information when quizzed on it later, because they knew they could find it on their computers. In the same study, a group was asked to remember both the information and the folders it was stored in. ==They didn’t remember the information, but they **remembered how to find the folders**.== …

questions.stem: Sparrow’s study shows that with the Internet, the human brain will ______.
basis: 首句就是 Sparrow 的结论：互联网改变的只是我们记什么，而不是记忆的能力。实验里，知道信息会被保存的人不去记信息本身；要求同时记信息和文件夹的人，没记住信息，却记住了怎么找文件夹。记的东西从“内容”变成了“去哪儿找”，就是记忆的重点转移了。
map: changing merely what we remember
switch its focus of memory

wrong.text: 实验没有涉及详细分析信息。
参与者记住的是信息存在哪里，不是更高效地收集信息。
原文说记忆能力没变（not our capacity），没说记忆时间会延长。

context.text: In a very practical way, ==the Internet is becoming **an external hard drive for our memories**, a process known as “cognitive offloading.”== Traditionally, this role was fulfilled by data banks, libraries, and other humans. ==Your father may never remember birthdays **because your mother does**, for instance.== …

questions.stem: The process of “cognitive offloading” ______.

options.C: enables us to classify trivial facts

basis: “认知卸载”就是把互联网当作记忆的外接硬盘。传统上这个角色由数据库、图书馆和别人承担，比如爸爸从来不记生日，因为妈妈记着。把要记的东西交给外部去存，就是减轻自己的记忆负担。offload 本义就是“卸下负担”。
map: an external hard drive for our memories
lessens our memory burdens

wrong.text: 没有提识别虚假信息。
“记忆没有退化”是 Sparrow 对实验结果的解读，认知卸载讲的是把记忆交给外部，不是防止记忆衰退。
实验里的 factoids 是琐碎事实，但没说认知卸载帮我们给它们分类。

context.text: … ==Some worry that this is having a destructive effect on society, **but Sparrow sees an upside**.== Perhaps, she suggests, ==the trend will **change our approach to learning** from a focus on individual facts and memorization to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking==—something that is not available on the Internet. “I personally have never seen all that much intellectual value in memorizing things,” Sparrow says, adding that we haven’t lost our ability to do it.

questions.stem: Which of the following would Sparrow support about the Internet?

options.A: It may reform our learning approach.
options.B: It may impact our society negatively.
options.C: It may enhance our adaptability to technology.
options.D: It may interfere with our conceptual thinking.

questions.answerZh: 它可能改革我们的学习方式
basis: 有人担心认知卸载对社会有破坏作用，但 Sparrow 看到了好的一面：这一趋势或许会把学习方式从注重单个事实和死记，转向更注重概念性思维。change our approach to learning 就是改革学习方式。
map: change our approach to learning
reform our learning approach

wrong.text: 认为对社会有破坏作用的是 Some（一些人），Sparrow 恰恰持相反态度。
第一段说的是人类记忆在“适应新的通讯技术”，是记忆在适应，不是互联网提高了我们对技术的适应能力。
Sparrow 认为学习会更强调概念性思维，而且这种思维是互联网上没有的，不是互联网干扰它。

context.text: ==Still other experts say it’s **too soon to understand** how the Internet affects our brains.== ==There is **no experimental evidence**== showing that it interferes with our ability to focus, for instance, wrote psychologists Christopher Chabris and Daniel J. Simons. …

questions.stem: It is indicated in Paragraph 3 that how the Internet affects our brains ______.

options.B: is most studied in older adults
options.C: is reflected in our reading speed

questions.answerZh: 需要进一步的学术研究
basis: 第三段首句是段落主旨：还有专家说，要弄清互联网如何影响大脑还为时过早。接着举例：没有实验证据表明上网会干扰专注力。现在下结论太早、证据不足，就是需要进一步研究。
map: too soon to understand / no experimental evidence
requires further academic research

wrong.text: 只提到 2008 年一项 24 人参与的老年人研究，不能说老年人被研究得最多。
那项研究比较的是上网和阅读哪个更能锻炼大脑，与阅读速度无关。
没有说影响取决于上网习惯。

context.text: … In other words, ==human memory is **not deteriorating**== but “adapting to new communications technology,” Sparrow says.

“There may be costs associated with our increased reliance on the Internet, ==but I’d have to imagine that overall **the benefits are going to outweigh those costs**==,” observes psychology professor Benjamin Storm. …

questions.stem: Neither Sparrow nor Storm would agree that ______.

options.A: our reliance on the Internet will be costly
options.B: the Internet is weakening our memory
options.C: memory exercise is a must for our brains
options.D: our ability to focus declines with age

questions.answerZh: 互联网正在削弱我们的记忆力
basis: Sparrow 明确说人类记忆没有退化（not deteriorating），只是在适应新技术；Storm 认为总体来看依赖互联网的好处会超过代价。两人对互联网与记忆都持积极态度，都不会同意“互联网在削弱记忆力”。
map: memory is not deteriorating
（不同意）the Internet is weakening our memory
questions.note: Neither … nor … would agree 是反向题：找两人都反对的说法。先确认两人的共同立场（都看好互联网对记忆的影响），再找与之相反的选项。

wrong.text: Storm 承认 There may be costs，他会部分同意依赖互联网有代价，所以不是两人都不同意。
Sparrow 认为死记硬背没多大价值，但没讨论“记忆锻炼”；Storm 也没谈，无法判断两人都反对。
专注力是第三段 Chabris 和 Simons 谈的，而且没有涉及年龄。

context.text: ==Teenagers are **paradoxical**.== That’s a mild and detached way of saying something that parents often express with considerably stronger language. But the paradox is scientific as well as personal. In adolescence, ==**helpless and dependent** children who have relied on grown-ups for just about everything become **independent** people== who can take care of themselves and help each other. At the same time, ==once **cheerful and compliant** children become **rebellious** teenage risk-takers==.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, children growing into adolescence tend to ______.

options.B: see the world in an unreasonable way
options.C: have fond memories of their past

questions.answerZh: 发展出相反的性格特征
basis: 首句定调：青少年是矛盾的（paradoxical）。后面给出两组变化：无助依赖的孩子变得独立、能照顾自己和帮助别人；与此同时，原本开朗顺从的孩子变成叛逆、爱冒险的青少年。一边变好、一边变“坏”，同时发展出相反的性格特征。
map: paradoxical
opposite personality traits

wrong.text: 没说青少年看待世界的方式不合理。
没有提对过去的回忆。
第二句说父母常用强烈得多的言辞形容青少年，是父母的抱怨，不是孩子对父母表达爱意。

context.text: … ==The study is part of **a new wave of thinking** about adolescence.== For a long time, scientists and policy makers concentrated on the idea that teenagers were a problem that needed to be solved. ==The new work emphasizes that adolescence is a time of **opportunity as well as risk**.==

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 2 that Crone’s study ______.

options.C: provides a new insight into adolescence

questions.answerZh: 为认识青春期提供了新视角
basis: 第二段说 Crone 的研究属于关于青春期的“新一波思考”。过去科学家和政策制定者把青少年看作需要解决的问题；新研究强调青春期既有风险也是机遇。这就是对青春期的新见解。
map: a new wave of thinking about adolescence
a new insight into adolescence

wrong.text: 没有讨论青少年的社会责任。
研究的是亲社会和叛逆行为，不是情绪问题。
只看负面、把青少年当问题是旧观点；新研究强调正负两面并存，还有机遇。

context.text: Other studies have shown that ==rebellious behavior **increases as you become a teenager** and then **fades away as you grow older**==. But the new study shows that, interestingly, ==**the same pattern** holds for prosocial behavior==. ==Teenagers were **more likely than younger children or adults** to report== that they did things like unselfishly help a friend. …

questions.stem: What does Crone’s study find about prosocial behavior?

options.A: It results from the wish to cooperate.
options.C: It is subject to family influence.
options.D: It tends to peak in adolescence.

questions.answerZh: 往往在青春期达到顶峰
basis: 第四段：其他研究发现，叛逆行为进入青春期时增多，长大后消退。新研究发现亲社会行为也是同样的模式（the same pattern），青少年比更小的孩子和成年人更常做无私帮助朋友这类事。先升后降、青春期最多，就是在青春期达到顶峰。最后一段也印证：奖励敏感度和亲社会行为、冒险一样，青春期上升、之后下降。
map: the same pattern（青春期增多，之后消退）
tends to peak in adolescence

wrong.text: 没有说亲社会行为源于合作的愿望。
没有提教育。
没有提家庭影响。

context.text: ==Teenagers are **particularly sensitive to social rewards**—winning the game, impressing a new friend, getting that boy to notice you.== Reward sensitivity, like prosocial behavior and risk-taking, seems to go up in adolescence and then down again as we age. …

questions.stem: It can be learned from the last two paragraphs that teenagers ______.

options.B: care a lot about social recognition
options.D: endeavor to live a joyful life

basis: 倒数第二段引出“奖励敏感度”；最后一段说青少年对社交奖励特别敏感，例子是赢得比赛、给新朋友留下好印象、让那个男孩注意到你，都是想得到别人的认可。所以青少年非常在意社会认可。
map: particularly sensitive to social rewards
care a lot about social recognition

wrong.text: 给新朋友留下印象是青少年想得到的奖励，不是夸大自己对别人的影响。
没有提对未来的焦虑。
派对上会发生新鲜刺激事情的例子说的是 30 岁以后的人懒得起身，用来对比奖励敏感度下降，不是说青少年努力过快乐的生活。

context.text: ==Teenagers are **paradoxical**.== …

Most significantly, ==there was a **positive correlation** between prosociality and rebelliousness==. The teenagers who were more rebellious were also more likely to help others. The good and bad sides of adolescence seem to develop together. …
==Is there some **common factor** that underlies these apparently **contradictory developments**?== …

questions.stem: What is the text mainly about?
questions.answerZh: 青少年为什么自相矛盾
basis: 首句提出论点：青少年是矛盾的。中间用 Crone 的研究说明正面和负面特质同时发展、而且正相关；第六段问这些看似矛盾的发展背后是否有共同因素，再用“奖励敏感度”来解释。全文就是在讲青少年为什么会自相矛盾。
map: paradoxical / contradictory developments
self-contradictory

wrong.text: 文章讲的是对奖励（reward）敏感，而且尤其是社交奖励，不是对风险敏感。
亲社会性只是矛盾的一面，文章同时讲叛逆。
变得独立只在第一段作为例子出现。

context.text: … ==This all seems random, but it’s **by design**==, part of what the $6.1 billion U.S. egg industry bets will be its next big thing: climate-friendly eggs.

These eggs, which are making their debut now on shelves for as much as $8 a dozen, are still labeled organic and animal-friendly, but ==they’re also from birds that live on **farms using regenerative agriculture**—**special techniques** to cultivate rich soils that can trap greenhouse gases==. …

questions.stem: The climate-friendly eggs are produced ______.

options.B: at the demand of regular shoppers
options.C: as a replacement for organic eggs

basis: 第一段说鸡群看似随意散放，其实是精心设计的（by design）。第二段解释：这些蛋来自采用再生农业的农场，再生农业就是用特殊技术培育能吸收温室气体的肥沃土壤。按特殊方法设计运营的农场，就是专门设计的农场。
map: by design / farms using regenerative agriculture—special techniques
on specially designed farms

wrong.text: 这种蛋卖到 8 美元一打，是高价产品。
没说是应普通顾客要求生产的。
这些蛋仍然贴着有机标签，是在有机之上再加一层，不是取代有机蛋。

context.text: “I’m excited about our progress,” says Brown, who harvests eggs for Denver-based NestFresh Eggs and is ==adding more cover crops that draw worms and crickets **for the chickens to eat**==. ==The birds’ waste then **fertilizes fields**.== Such improvements “allow our hens to forage for higher-quality natural feed that will be ==**good for the land, the hens, and the eggs**== that we supply to our customers.”

questions.stem: Larry Brown is excited about his progress in ______.
questions.answerZh: 建立了一个可持续的系统
basis: 第三段描述 Brown 的进展：多种覆盖作物，引来蠕虫和蟋蟀给鸡吃；鸡粪再给田地施肥；母鸡吃到更好的天然饲料，对土地、母鸡和鸡蛋都有好处。作物养虫、虫喂鸡、鸡粪肥田，形成一个循环，就是可持续的系统。
map: cover crops → worms → chickens → waste fertilizes fields
a sustainable system

wrong.text: 种覆盖作物是为了吸引蠕虫给鸡当食物，不是减少虫害。
鸡粪是用来肥田的，不是加速处理废物。
没有谈吸引顾客。

context.text: The egg industry’s push is the first major test of whether animal products from regenerative farms can become the next premium offering. In barely more than a decade, ==organic eggs went from being **dismissed as a niche product** in natural foods stores to **being sold at Walmart**==. More recently there were similar doubts about probiotics and plant-based meats, but both have exploded into major supermarket categories. ==If the sustainable-egg rollout is successful, it could **open the floodgates** for regenerative beef, broccoli, and beyond.==

questions.stem: The example of organic eggs is used in Paragraph 4 to suggest ______.

options.B: the setbacks in the egg industry

basis: 第四段首句提出：鸡蛋业的这次推广，是检验再生农场的动物产品能否成为下一个高端产品的第一场大考。接着举例：有机蛋十来年间从小众产品变成沃尔玛货架上的商品；益生菌、植物肉也一样。如果可持续鸡蛋成功，就会为再生牛肉、西兰花等打开闸门。举有机蛋的成功，是为了说明再生产品也有这样的潜力。
map: dismissed as a niche product → being sold at Walmart / open the floodgates
the potential of regenerative products

wrong.text: 质疑只是起点，例子要说明的是质疑之后的成功。
有机蛋讲的是成功，不是挫折。
沃尔玛只是有机蛋走向主流的标志，例子不是在讲超市的促销。

context.text: The industry is betting that ==the same consumers paying more for premium attributes such as free-range, non-GMO, and pasture-raised eggs **will embrace sustainability**==. Surveys show that ==younger generations are **more concerned about climate change**==, and some of the success of plant-based meat can be chalked up to shoppers wanting to signal their desire to protect the environment. ==Young adults “**really care about the planet**,”== says John Brunnquell, president of Egg Innovations. …

questions.stem: It can be learned from the last paragraph that young people ______.

options.A: are reluctant to change their diet
options.B: are likely to buy climate-friendly eggs

questions.answerZh: 很可能会购买气候友好型鸡蛋
basis: 最后一段：行业押注那些愿意为高端属性多花钱的消费者也会接受可持续理念；调查显示年轻一代更关心气候变化，植物肉的成功部分就是因为购物者想表明自己要保护环境；Egg Innovations 的总裁说年轻人“真的很在乎地球”。所以年轻人很可能会买气候友好型鸡蛋。
map: more concerned about climate change / really care about the planet
likely to buy climate-friendly eggs

wrong.text: 原文说年轻人正在改变食物链，并不抗拒改变。
没有说年轻人对新食物好奇。
没有说他们对农业进步感到惊讶。

context.text: ==Regenerative products could be **a hard sell**==, because the concept is tough to define quickly, says Julie Stanton, associate professor of agricultural economics at Pennsylvania State University Brandywine. …

… Young adults “really care about the planet,” says John Brunnquell, president of Egg Innovations. ==“They are **absolutely altering the food chain** beyond what I think even they understand what they’re doing.”==

questions.stem: John Brunnquell would disagree with Julie Stanton over regenerative products’ ______.
basis: Stanton（第五段）认为再生产品可能很难卖（a hard sell），因为概念很难一下子讲清楚。Brunnquell（第六段）则说年轻人真的在乎地球，正在彻底改变食物链，对市场很乐观。一个看衰销路、一个看好销路，分歧在市场前景。
map: a hard sell ↔ absolutely altering the food chain
market prospects

wrong.text: Stanton 提到再生农业对食品本身几乎没有改进，但 Brunnquell 没谈营养，看不出分歧。
“概念难定义”是 Stanton 说难卖的理由，Brunnquell 没有就定义发表看法。
两人都没谈道德含义。

context.text: ==One in three Americans who are at least 40 have or **plan to have a job in retirement**== to prepare for a longer life, according to a survey conducted by Harris Poll for TD Ameritrade. Even more surprising is that more than half of “unretirees”—those who plan to work in retirement or went back to work after retiring—==said they **would be employed in their later years** even if they had enough money to settle down==, the survey showed.

questions.stem: The survey conducted by Harris Poll indicates that ______.

options.A: over half of the retirees are physically fit for work
options.B: the old workforce is as active as the younger one
options.C: one in three Americans enjoy earlier retirement
options.D: more Americans are willing to work in retirement

questions.answerZh: 更多美国人愿意在退休后继续工作
basis: 第二段的调查结果：40 岁以上的美国人中，三分之一已经或打算在退休后工作；更令人意外的是，一半以上的“不退休者”说即使钱够了，晚年也还会工作。这和首段“越来越多美国人选择退休后继续工作”一致。
map: have, or plan to have a job in retirement / would be employed … even if they had enough money
willing to work in retirement

wrong.text: “一半以上”说的是不退休者即使有钱也会工作，不是身体适合工作。
没有比较老年和年轻劳动力的活跃程度。
三分之一的人是打算在退休后工作，不是享受提前退休。

context.text: … Other reasons, according to the study, include ==personal fulfillment such as **staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression**==. About 72% of “unretiree” respondents said that they would return to work once retired to keep mentally fit while 59% said it would be tied to making ends meet.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from Paragraph 3 that Americans tend to think that ______.

options.A: retirement may cause problems for them
options.B: boredom can be relieved after retirement
options.C: the mental health of retirees is overlooked

questions.answerZh: 退休可能给他们带来问题
basis: 第三段：钱不是“不退休”的唯一原因，其他原因包括保持头脑健康、防止无聊、避免抑郁。人们继续工作是为了避开这些问题，说明他们认为退休可能带来这些问题。
map: staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression
retirement may cause problems

wrong.text: 人们继续工作是为了防止无聊，说明他们认为退休会无聊，而不是退休后无聊会缓解。
没有说退休者的心理健康被忽视。
没有谈对经济的贡献。

context.text: ==One reason for the change in retirement patterns: **Americans are living longer**.== …

questions.stem: Retirement patterns are changing partly due to ______.
basis: 第五段首句直接给出原因：退休模式变化的一个原因是美国人更长寿了。one reason 对应题干 partly。
map: One reason for the change in retirement patterns
Retirement patterns are changing partly due to
Americans are living longer
longer life expectancy

wrong.text: 没有提劳动力短缺。
原文说老年人是劳动力中增长最快的群体，不是人口增长。
第七段说有人担心晚年入不敷出，但没说生活成本在上涨。

context.text: … ==Six in 10 “unretirees” are **increasing their savings** in anticipation of a longer life, according to the survey.== Among the most popular ways they are doing this, the company said, is by ==**reducing their overall expenses**==, securing life insurance or maximizing their contributions to retirement accounts.

questions.stem: Many “unretirees” are increasing their savings by ______.
basis: 第六段：十分之六的不退休者在增加储蓄，最常见的方式是削减总体开支、买人寿保险、尽量多往退休账户里存钱。reducing their overall expenses 就是少花钱。
map: reducing their overall expenses
spending less

wrong.text: 原文是往退休账户存钱和买保险，没说投资股票。
没有提打零工。
没有提找高薪工作。

context.text: Unfortunately, many people who are opting to work in retirement are preparing to do so because ==they are **worried about making ends meet** in their later years==, said Brent Weiss, a co-founder at Baltimore-based financial-planning firm Facet Wealth. He suggested that preretirees should ==**speak with a financial adviser** to set long-term financial goals==.
… “It’s not just a financial decision, but an emotional one. ==Many people believe they **can’t retire**.==”

questions.stem: With regard to retirement, Brent Weiss thinks that many people are ______.
basis: 第七段：Weiss 说遗憾的是，很多人打算退休后工作，是因为担心晚年入不敷出；他建议准退休者找理财顾问定长期目标。最后一段又说退休是人生最难的时刻之一，很多人觉得自己退不了休。钱没攒够、需要找顾问规划，说明很多人对退休没有准备好。
map: worried about making ends meet / believe they can’t retire
unprepared

wrong.text: 他们担心晚年生计，并非无所畏惧。
没有说失望。
人们是担忧而非热情。

context.text: … Something that should be simple and transparent can be complicated, intentionally or unintentionally, ==in ways that **impair consumer choice**==. These are examples of dark patterns.

First coined in 2010 by user experience expert Harry Brignull, “dark patterns” is a catch-all term for ==practices that manipulate user interfaces to **influence the decision-making ability of users**==. …

questions.stem: It can be learned from the first two paragraphs that dark patterns ______.
basis: 第一段说本该简单透明的事被弄得复杂，损害了消费者的选择；第二段定义暗黑模式：操纵用户界面、影响用户决策能力的做法。损害选择、操纵决策，就是削弱用户的决策。
map: impair consumer choice / manipulate … to influence the decision-making ability
undermine users’ decision-making

wrong.text: 暗黑模式让用户感到被骗、受挫，不是改善体验。
前两段没有提泄露用户信息。
隐藏费用是暗黑模式的一种，它是在隐藏费用，不是提醒用户。

context.text: In a 2019 study of 53,000 product pages and 11,000 websites, ==researchers found that **about one in 10 employs** these design practices==. ==Though **widely prevalent**==, the concept of dark patterns is still not well understood. …

questions.stem: The 2019 study on dark patterns is mentioned to show ______.
basis: 第三段：2019 年一项覆盖 5.3 万个产品页面、1.1 万个网站的研究发现，约十分之一采用了这些设计。下一句直接总结为“虽然非常普遍”（widely prevalent）。研究数据就是用来说明暗黑模式随处可见。
map: widely prevalent
their strong presence

wrong.text: 研究没有讲暗黑模式的缺陷。
没有讲设计复杂。
研究给出的是普遍程度，不是危害程度。

context.text: … ==Businesses should **engage in conversations with** IT, compliance, risk, and legal teams== to review their privacy policy, and include in the discussion the customer/user experience designers and coders responsible for the company’s user interface, as well as the marketers and advertisers responsible for sign-ups, checkout baskets, pricing, and promotions. ==Any or all these teams can play a role in **creating or avoiding “digital deception.”**==

questions.stem: To handle digital deception, businesses should ______.
basis: 第四段：企业应与 IT、合规、风控和法务团队对话，审查隐私政策，并让负责界面的设计师和程序员、负责注册和定价促销的营销人员也参与讨论；这些团队都可能制造或避免“数字欺骗”。和这些团队谈，就是与相关团队沟通。
map: engage in conversations with … teams
talk with relevant teams

wrong.text: 参与讨论的是用户体验设计师，不是听取顾客反馈。
原文说的都是企业内部团队，不是外部独立机构。
没有提专业培训。

context.text: … In March, the California Attorney General announced the approval of additional regulations under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) that ==“ensure that consumers **will not be confused or misled** when seeking to exercise their data privacy rights.”== ==The regulations aim to **ban dark patterns**==—this means prohibiting companies from using “confusing language or unnecessary steps such as forcing them to click through multiple screens or listen to reasons why they shouldn’t opt out.”

questions.stem: The additional regulations under the CCPA are intended to ______.
basis: 第五段：加州总检察长批准的补充规定旨在“确保消费者在行使数据隐私权时不会被迷惑或误导”，目的就是禁止暗黑模式。不被迷惑、误导，就是不被欺骗。
map: will not be confused or misled
protect consumers from being tricked

wrong.text: 规定禁止企业在用户退出时设置多余步骤，不是去引导用户完成退出。
数据隐私权是消费者的，不是授予企业的。
没有提限制访问问题内容。

context.text: As more states consider promulgating additional regulations, ==there is a need for **greater accountability from within the business community**==. ==Dark patterns also can be addressed on a **self-regulatory basis**, but only if organizations **hold themselves accountable**==, not just to legal requirements but also to industry best practices and standards.

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, a key to coping with dark patterns is ______.
basis: 最后一段：越来越多的州考虑出台新规，但企业界内部需要更多担当。暗黑模式也可以靠自我监管来解决，前提是企业对自己负责，不只是满足法律要求，还要遵守行业最佳实践和标准。自我监管、自己担责，就是企业自律。
map: self-regulatory basis / hold themselves accountable
businesses’ self-discipline

wrong.text: 原文强调不能只满足法律要求（not just to legal requirements）。
原文说的是行业最佳实践和标准，不是严格的监管标准。
最后一段没有谈消费者的安全意识。

context.text: Although ethics classes are common around the world, ==**scientists are unsure** if their lessons can actually change behavior; **evidence either way is weak**==, relying on contrived laboratory tests or sometimes unreliable self-reports. …

questions.stem: Scientists generally believe that the effects of ethics classes are ______.
basis: 首句：尽管伦理课在世界各地都很常见，科学家并不确定这些课能否真正改变行为，正反两方面的证据都很弱，依赖的是人为设计的实验室测试或有时不可靠的自我报告。不确定、证据弱，就是效果难以确定。
map: are unsure / evidence either way is weak
hard to determine

wrong.text: 没说效果被狭隘地解读。
效果本身都不确定，谈不上难以忽视。
没说总结得不好。

context.text: … They chose this particular behavior for three reasons, according to study co-author Eric Schwitzgebel, a philosopher at the University of California, Riverside: students’ attitudes on the topic are variable and unstable, ==behavior is **easily measurable**==, and ethics literature largely agrees that eating less meat is good because it reduces environmental harm and animal suffering. …

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason for the researchers to study meat-eating?

options.B: It is a behavior easy to measure.
options.C: It is important to students’ health.
options.D: It is a hot topic in ethics classes.

basis: 第二段列出三个理由：学生对这个话题的态度多变且不稳定；这种行为容易测量；伦理学文献大体认为少吃肉是好事，因为能减少环境危害和动物痛苦。第二条就是 B。
map: behavior is easily measurable
a behavior easy to measure

wrong.text: 原文说的是学生的态度多变，不是吃肉在学生中很普遍。
少吃肉的好处是减少环境危害和动物痛苦，不是学生健康。
没说它是伦理课上的热门话题。

context.text: Schwitzgebel predicted the intervention would have no effect; he had previously found that ==ethics professors **do not differ from other professors** on a range of behaviors, including voting rates, blood donation and returning library books==. …

questions.stem: Eric Schwitzgebel’s previous findings suggest that ethics professors ______.

options.A: are seldom critical of their students
options.B: are less sociable than other professors
options.C: are not sensitive to political issues

basis: 第三段：Schwitzgebel 原本预测干预不会有效果，因为他此前发现，伦理学教授在投票、献血、归还图书馆的书等一系列行为上，和其他教授没有差别。懂伦理的人行为并不比别人更有道德，这就是“不一定更有道德”。
map: do not differ from other professors on a range of behaviors
not necessarily ethically better

wrong.text: 没有提他们对学生的批评。
没有比较社交能力。
投票率只是用来比较行为的一个例子，不能推出对政治问题不敏感。

context.text: … Psychologist Nina Strohminger at the University of Pennsylvania, who was not involved in the study, says ==she wants the effect to be real but **cannot rule out some unknown confounding variable**==. And if real, she notes, ==it might be **reversible** by another nudge==: “Easy come, easy go.”

questions.stem: Nina Strohminger thinks that the effect of the intervention is ______.
basis: 第四段：Strohminger 希望这个效果是真的，但无法排除某个未知的干扰变量；而且即使是真的，也可能被另一次“助推”逆转，来得容易去得也快。效果是否真实、能否持续都说不准，就是不确定。
map: cannot rule out some unknown confounding variable / might be reversible
uncertain

wrong.text: 她说效果可能被逆转，不是永久的。
做出预测的是 Schwitzgebel，而且他预测错了；Strohminger 没谈可预测性。
她说的是效果可能被逆转（reversible），不是无法重复。

context.text: Schwitzgebel suspects ==the greatest impact came from **social influence**==—classmates or teaching assistants leading the discussions may have shared their own vegetarianism, showing it as achievable or more common. ==**Second**, the video may have had an emotional impact.== ==**Least rousing**, he thinks, was rational argument==, although his co-authors say reason might play a bigger role. …

questions.stem: Eric Schwitzgebel suspects that the students’ change in behavior ______.

options.C: is a result of multiple factors

questions.answerZh: 是多种因素共同作用的结果
basis: 最后一段：Schwitzgebel 认为影响最大的是社会影响（同学或助教可能分享了自己吃素的经历）；其次是视频的情感冲击；作用最小的是理性论证。最大、其次、最小，列出了好几个因素，所以行为改变是多因素的结果。
map: the greatest … / Second … / Least rousing …
a result of multiple factors

wrong.text: 视频带来的情感冲击是原因之一，不是行为改变带来的心理好处。
研究确实用了餐卡数据，但这一段讲的是原因，不是能否做统计分析。
没有说这是自我发展的标志。

context.text: … We know ==we are moving into a period where the jobs in demand will **change rapidly**==, as will the requirements of the jobs that remain. Research by the World Economic Forum finds that ==on average 42 per cent of the “core skills” within job roles **will change by 2022**==. ==That is a **very short timeline**==.

questions.stem: Research by the World Economic Forum suggests ______.

options.C: a steady growth of job opportunities
options.D: an urgent demand for new job skills

questions.answerZh: 对新工作技能的迫切需求
basis: 根据题干的 World Economic Forum 定位到第一段第三句：到 2022 年，各岗位平均 42% 的“核心技能”都会改变（will change by 2022）。前一句说需求岗位会迅速变化（change rapidly），后一句强调时间非常紧（a very short timeline）。岗位技能很快要变，说明对新工作技能的需求很迫切。
map: 42 per cent of the “core skills” … will change by 2022 / a very short timeline
an urgent demand for new job skills

wrong.text: 首句说不想让潜在劳动力掉队，没有提到全职就业会增加。
研究说核心技能会改变，没有说人们对核心技能有争议。
原文说岗位需求会迅速变化，不是就业机会稳定增长。

context.text: … For individual companies, ==the temptation is always to **let go of workers**== whose skills are no longer in demand and replace them with those whose skills are. ==That **does not always happen**==. AT&T is often given as the gold standard of a company who decided to do ==a massive reskilling program **rather than** go with a fire-and-hire strategy==. …

questions.stem: AT&T is cited to show ______.

options.A: an alternative to the fire-and-hire strategy
options.B: an immediate need for government support
options.C: the importance of staff appraisal standards

questions.answerZh: 解雇再雇佣策略的替代方案
basis: 第二段：对单个公司来说，常见做法是解雇技能过时的员工，再换上有所需技能的人，即“先裁后招”。接着话锋一转：情况并不总是这样（That does not always happen）。AT&T 被视为典范，它选择了大规模的技能再培训，而不是先裁后招（rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy）。引用 AT&T 是为了说明“先裁后招”之外还有另一种做法。
map: a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy
an alternative to the fire-and-hire strategy

wrong.text: 求助政府是第二段后半讲的宏观层面，AT&T 是公司层面的例子。
原文没有讨论员工考核标准。
AT&T 的例子是为了说明再培训可以替代先裁后招，不是介绍再培训项目有什么特点。

context.text: … ==Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably **languid at best**==, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of ==employers **begging for workers**==, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high.

questions.stem: Efforts to resolve the skills mismatch in Canada ______.
basis: 第二段末句：加拿大和其他地方解决技能错配的努力，充其量只能说是迟缓无力的（languid at best），结果失业率高的时候和地区，雇主照样在求着招人。努力没能解决问题，说明这些努力不够。
map: arguably languid at best
have appeared to be insufficient

wrong.text: 原文只说雇主急着招人，没有说劳动力成本被推高。
原文没有提到有人反对这些努力。
“失业率高还缺人”是努力不力造成的矛盾局面，不是说努力本身前后不一致。

context.text: … As of May, those rates had spiked up to 13.3 per cent and 13.7 per cent, and ==although many worker shortages had disappeared, **not all had done so**==. In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that ==there were still **clear shortages** of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel==.

questions.stem: We can learn from Paragraph 3 that there was ______.
basis: 第三段：疫情下失业率飙升，很多岗位的缺人问题消失了，但并非全部如此（not all had done so）。接着举例：医疗领域仍然明显缺少医生、护士和其他医务人员（clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel）。第三段讲的就是医务人员短缺。
map: clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel
a lack of medical workers

wrong.text: 第三段只讲失业率和缺人的情况，没有人呼吁调整政策。
失业率从二月的低点飙升到五月的高点，说明经济在恶化，不是复苏。
很多岗位不再缺人是疫情导致的现象，原文没有说招聘做法发生了变化。

context.text: … That seems to be the case in Sweden: ==When forced to **furlough** 90 per cent of their cabin staff==, Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that ==**reskilled the laid-off workers** to **support hospital staff**==. The effort was a collective one and involved other companies as well as a Swedish university.

questions.stem: Scandinavian Airlines decided to ______.

options.A: retrain their cabin staff for better services
options.B: create job vacancies for the unemployed
options.D: prepare their laid-off workers for other jobs

questions.answerZh: 培训被裁员工从事其他工作

context.text: If you’re not convinced of the inherent value in taking a year off to explore interests, then ==consider its **financial impact** on future **academic choices**==.
